body.statement:
At every two-sided pathwise-interior \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), for every coherent foldwise fit whose raw measurement matrices are thresholded and renormalized before any bridge or projection object is formed, if \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\), then on an event whose probability tends to one,
\[
 \|E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n,
 \qquad
 \Delta_n=r_m(r_\pi+r_A^c+r_Z^c)+r_A^cr_Z^c
 +(r_A^c+r_Z^c)R_\Sigma.
\]
Here \(\widehat m_j=\int_{\mathcal Y}y\widehat f_jd\nu\), and \(r_B,\ldots,r_b\) refer to the cleaned-law plug-ins.  In particular, the pathwise derivative of the mean bias is zero along a support-preserving two-sided perturbation of \(M_A\) alone and along a coherent perturbation of \(f\) alone.
body.justification: The corrected expansion uses \(\bar M_A^{-1}M_A-I\) and \(\bar M_Z^{-1}M_Z-I\), so coherent support cleaning leaves only products of cleaned errors.
body.gap: The neighboring binary and categorical results do not cover this cleaned multilevel posterior-and-Gram correction.
body.consumer: It provides the explicit second-order remainder used by the cross-fitted estimator.
body.proof_tex:
Work coordinatewise and set \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\).  By the support-cleaning conditional-zero lemma, \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\) produces an event \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\) of probability tending to one on which
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \left[(r_A^c+r_Z^c)\|\widehat k-k\|_2+r_A^cr_Z^c\right].       \tag{69}
\]
The cleaned score-stability lemma gives \(\|\widehat k-k\|_2\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma\).  Consequently,
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \{(r_A^c+r_Z^c)R_\Sigma+r_A^cr_Z^c\}.                         \tag{70}
\]

We next calculate the raw bridge mean.  The bridges in \(\widehat U\) are formed from \(\bar M_A\) and \(\bar M_Z\).  For \(j,\ell\in\mathcal J\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \delta^A_{j\ell}(X)
 &=E_P\{\bar a_j(A,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\},\\
 \delta^Z_{j\ell}(X)
 &=E_P\{\bar z_j(Z,X)\mid J=\ell,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=\ell\}.
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{71}
\]
The bridge definition and the true measurement laws give the exact matrix identities
\[
 \delta^A=\bar M_A^{-1}M_A-I_K=\bar M_A^{-1}(M_A-\bar M_A),
 \qquad
 \delta^Z=\bar M_Z^{-1}M_Z-I_K=\bar M_Z^{-1}(M_Z-\bar M_Z).     \tag{72}
\]
The cleaned fitted singular-value half-margins and the cleaning bounds imply
\[
 \|\delta^A\|_{L^2(P_X)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^c,
 \qquad
 \|\delta^Z\|_{L^2(P_X)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^c,            \tag{73}
\]
and both matrices are uniformly bounded.

By three-view conditional independence, conditional on \((J=\ell,X)\), the factors \(Y,A,Z\) separate.  Since \(\widehat m_j(x)=\int y\widehat f_j(y\mid x)d\nu(y)\),
\(E_P(Y-\widehat m_j\mid J=\ell,X)=m_\ell-\widehat m_j\).  Expanding \(\widehat U_j\), conditioning first on \((J,X)\), and summing over \(J\) yields the exact equality
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P(\widehat U_j\mid X)-m_j
={}&(\widehat m_j-m_j)
 \left[1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}
 (1+\delta^A_{jj})(1+\delta^Z_{jj})\right]\\
&+\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\sum_{\ell\ne j}\pi_\ell
 \delta^A_{j\ell}\delta^Z_{j\ell}(m_\ell-\widehat m_j).       \tag{74}
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(\ell=j\), both bridge means equal one plus their errors; for \(\ell\ne j\), both indicator terms are zero, which proves (74) without approximation.

Latent positivity and the fitted propensity half-margin give \(\pi_j^{-1}\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\) and \(\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\leq2\varepsilon^{-1}\).  The declared common bounded support gives \(|m_\ell|\vee|\widehat m_j|\leq L\).  Also
\[
 \left|1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}\right|
 \leq2\varepsilon^{-1}|\widehat\pi_j-\pi_j|.                  \tag{75}
\]
Expanding the bracket in the first line of (74), using the uniform bounds on \(\delta^A,\delta^Z\), and applying Cauchy--Schwarz with (73) bounds its expectation by
\(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_m(r_\pi+r_A^c+r_Z^c)\).  Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the second line of (74) bounds its expectation by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^cr_Z^c\).  Since \(K\) is fixed and \(E_Pm_j(X)=\psi_j\),
\[
 \|E_P\widehat U-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}
 \{r_m(r_\pi+r_A^c+r_Z^c)+r_A^cr_Z^c\}.                       \tag{76}
\]
Finally,
\[
 E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi
 =(E_P\widehat U-\psi)-E_P\widehat k.
\]
Combining (70), (76), and the definition of \(\Delta_n\) proves the displayed bias bound on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\).

For the derivative assertions, let \(t\mapsto\eta_t\) be a support-preserving two-sided regular perturbation with \(\eta_0=\eta\), and evaluate the score mean under \(P=P_{\eta_0}\).  If only \(M_A\) varies, then \(m_t=m\), \(\pi_t=\pi\), and \(\delta_t^Z=0\).  Equation (74) gives
\[
 E_PU(\eta_t)-\psi=0.                                          \tag{77}
\]
Support preservation makes the true-zero discrepancy identically zero.  The conditional-zero calculation (64)--(68), with the \(Z\)-error equal to zero, gives
\[
 \|E_PQ(\eta_t)U(\eta_t)\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A(t)
 \|Q(\eta_t)U(\eta_t)-QU\|_2=O(t^2),                          \tag{78}
\]
because DQM differentiability gives \(r_A(t)=O(|t|)\), while the separated inverse and Gram-gap perturbation identities give score displacement \(O(|t|)\).  Equations (77)--(78) make the derivative at zero vanish.

If only \(f\) varies coherently, then \(M_A,M_Z,\pi\), and \(B\) are fixed, so \(\delta_t^A=\delta_t^Z=0\).  Equation (74) again gives \(E_PU(\eta_t)=\psi\).  Projector algebra gives \(B^{\mathsf T}N_t=0\), and each column of \(h_t=N_tc_t\) is in \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\); hence
\[
 B^{\mathsf T}\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\}=0.                             \tag{79}
\]
By three-view independence, the \(j\)-th coordinate of (79) is
\[
 E_P\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\mid Y,J=j,X\}
 =\sum_{a,z}B_{(a,z),j}\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\}_{az}(Y,X)=0.
\]
Iterated expectation gives \(E_PQ_tU(\eta_t)=0\) exactly.  Thus the mean bias is identically zero along the coherent \(f\)-only perturbation, proving the second derivative assertion.
